summary: South Korea admits citizens of the 111 countries and regions on the Ministry of Justice's K-ETA eligibility list (as of 7 October 2026) without a visa for 30–180 days, normally subject to the K-ETA electronic travel authorization (10,000 KRW, valid 3 years) — though K-ETA has been temporarily waived for 22 countries including the US, UK and Japan; other nationalities apply for a C-3 short-term visit visa at an embassy, a consulate or a designated visa application centre.

notes: Canada's travel advice says it is illegal to bring narcotic or psychotropic drugs into South Korea, even with a prescription, unless you have an import permit applied for online before you arrive.

The Korea Customs Service's duty-free allowance is goods worth up to USD 800 in total, plus, on top of that, alcohol of up to 2 litres and USD 400, 200 cigarettes, 20 ml of e-cigarette liquid nicotine and 100 ml of perfume; travellers under 19 get no allowance for alcohol or cigarettes.

The Korea Customs Service says meat, plants, fruit, vegetables and other agricultural, livestock and fishery products, including processed foods, must be declared on arrival. Goods over the allowance that are found undeclared carry an extra 40% on top of the duty.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa or K-ETA for South Korea?
faq.answer: US citizens do not need a visa for stays up to 90 days. A K-ETA is normally required, but it has been temporarily waived for US passport holders (along with 21 other countries), and the Ministry of Justice has extended the waiver to December 31, 2026.

faq.question: What is the K-ETA and how much does it cost?
faq.answer: The Korea Electronic Travel Authorization is an online pre-clearance for visa-free visitors, costing KRW 10,000 (about USD 7–8 according to the portal) plus a 3% online card-payment charge, and valid for 3 years for multiple visits. The portal says approval must be obtained before boarding and that assessment typically takes 72 hours or less. K-ETA holders also skip the arrival card at immigration.

faq.question: How long can Canadians stay in South Korea?
faq.answer: The K-ETA portal gives Canadian citizens an allowed stay of 6 months, the longest it lists. The K-ETA requirement is temporarily waived for Canadians, and the Ministry of Justice has extended the waiver to December 31, 2026.

faq.question: Can Chinese citizens visit South Korea without a visa?
faq.answer: Individual Chinese travelers need a C-3 short-term visit visa, except on Jeju, where the Ministry of Justice says Chinese nationals may travel visa-free for 30 days, individually or in groups. The Ministry of Justice announced a trial visa-free scheme for Chinese tour groups of 3 or more, recruited by designated agencies, for stays of up to 15 days, from 29 September 2025 to 30 June 2026; we have found no official notice extending it.

faq.question: How much does a South Korean tourist visa cost?
faq.answer: For nationalities that need one (including Indian, Filipino, Vietnamese and Indonesian citizens), the single-entry C-3 short-term visit visa costs USD 40 for stays up to 90 days; a double-entry visa costs USD 70 and an unlimited multiple-entry visa USD 90, as set by Article 71 of the Enforcement Rules of the Immigration Act. Missions collect the equivalent in local currency. Korean embassies and consulates issue it, under Article 9 of the same Enforcement Rules. The Korea Visa Portal lists designated visa application centres in 12 countries that accept applications on their behalf.
